idee_recherchee.texte: The holographic principle proposes that all the information contained in a volume of space can be encoded on its boundary surface, as if our three-dimensional universe were a projection from a two-dimensional surface.

titre: The Matrix et l'hypothèse de la simulation selon Vopson
resume: The Matrix popularized the idea that reality is a convincing illusion, which fits the simulation hypothesis of an artificial universe. Vopson's theory suggests the opposite of entropy, with information getting cleaner and more structured, as if the universe were a self-organizing program.
texte: Fast forward to the 20th century and along comes The Matrix where Keanu Reeves learns that, yep, reality [music] is just a super convincing illusion designed to keep us in line and kung [music] fu. In The Matrix, reality is just a high-tech simulation and humans are trapped inside of it without realizing it. >> [music] >> That fits right into the simulation hypothesis which says our universe might be an artificial construct [music] like a super advanced video game. Even though the second law of thermodynamics says everything should get more chaotic over time, Vopson's theory suggests the opposite might be happening. >> [music] >> If reality behaves less like a decaying physical system and more like a structured self-organizing program, then maybe that's because it is a program. Maybe our universe is running on some cosmic level code instead of breaking down like real-world physics [music] predicts, it's following simulation-like rules where things get more efficient and organized over time. If entropy is supposed to be king, but information is getting cleaner and more structured, maybe that's because we are in [music] the matrix or at least something a lot like it.
